subject: Discovery recap: policy slices & per-customer routing (next steps)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@fastlane.ai>
Cc: ops-team@fastlane.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: policy slices & per-customer routing (next steps)

Marcus — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment.

Key pain points you described
- High variance in per-customer token utilization making costs unpredictable for large retail partners.
- Need to enforce per-tenant QPS and burst limits to protect peak traffic (holiday sales spikes).
- Desire to route high-value customers to dedicated pools / premium model variants while keeping lower tiers on shared capacity.
- Compliance: audit logs for per-tenant requests and retention settings for different customer tiers.

Current stack notes you shared
- Edge API gateway in front of a mix of hosted LLM endpoints and customer-managed inference (some partners on GCP/private infra).
- Custom billing pipeline that currently aggregates tokens by account but lacks enforcement at the serving layer.

Success criteria you gave (rough)
- SLOs: p95 latency <= 220ms for premium tier; p95 <= 450ms for standard with clear fallbacks.
- Per-customer cost visibility and hard limits that prevent a single tenant from exhausting shared capacity.
- Deployment plan that keeps existing gateway unchanged for first phase; config-driven policy pushes.

Proposed Redwood approach (high-level)
- Per-tenant policy slices: token quotas, QPS limits, burst allowance, and model-variant routing rules.
- Smart routing: premium tenant traffic -> pinned dedicated pool or higher-capacity model; standard -> shared pool with prefix caching.
- Audit and retention controls surfaced in the Console + exportable logs for billing.

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Marcus: share a redacted top-10 tenant usage CSV (tokens/day, peak QPS) — helps us map tiers (by 1/15).
2) FastLane ops: confirm whether any tenants are on private infra that require VPC egress (cc: ops-team).
3) Jasmine (me): send a policy matrix template and a draft SLA for premium tier (attached).
4) Karthik (cc'd): technical deep-dive to validate latency and routing constraints — propose 1/19 for a 45-min session.

Attachments: [Attachment: policy-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 38KB)], [Attachment: SLA-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 14KB)]

If that matches your understanding I’ll queue the contract-facing SLA and loop in our solutions engineer for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — solid recap, that’s exactly what we discussed. A couple clarifications:

- The CSV you requested: I’ll export a 90-day window and remove PII. Should have it to you by EOD Friday (1/15).
- Private infra: two of our large partners (Axiom Retail & NorthHaven) are indeed on customer-managed instances and require VPC peering for any direct routing.
- For the SLA, can you include an option for soft-failover routing (route to lower-cost variant with a 10% latency penalty) vs. hard cutoff? Our ops team prefers softer degradation for a better customer experience.

We’re interested in the per-tenant audit logs — retention policies differ by partner (some demand 1 year, some 90 days). We’ll include retention tiers in the CSV.

Agree on the technical deep-dive; 1/19 works for us. Please include Karthik plus whoever owns routing at Redwood.

—Marcus

Looping Karthik in as requested — forwarding Jasmine’s recap + Marcus notes.

Quick internal notes:
- We’ll want to prepare three configuration patterns for the deep-dive:
  1) Premium pinned pool (dedicated GPUs, static routing rule)
  2) Shared pool with burst caps + KV prefix caching (cost-efficient)
  3) Hybrid: dedicated for hot paths + shared for background/async traffic
- For private infra tenants we need to confirm supported auth (mTLS vs. shared API key) and whether we can push routing policies via customer-controlled controllers.
- I’ll validate that our audit logs can be split by tenant and retention window via our Console export (should be fine, but need ops confirmation).

Karthik — can you bring one latency test case (p95 measurements for a 512-token gen) and a short note on KV cache warmup behavior for pinned vs. shared pools?

V.

Thanks for the context — I’ll prepare the items for 1/19. Preliminary notes:

- Latency baseline: p95 for 512-token generation on our current shared medium model is ~190ms in us-west; premium + quantized variants can hit ~140–160ms depending on batch size.
- Burst handling: we typically enforce a leaky-bucket QPS limiter per tenant with a configurable burst window. We can model a per-tenant token quota that replenishes over a 24h window or smaller windows for stricter enforcement.
- Routing mechanics: policy-driven routing rules are encoded as lightweight JSON policies in the control plane; can be pushed via API or configured in the Console. For private infra partners we can optionally expose a signed policy bundle that their controller will accept (mTLS recommended).

I’ll attach a lightweight policy template and a short test plan for the deep-dive (what I’ll demo: p95 before/after pinning, measured token cost delta, and cache-warmup effect).

Attachments: [Attachment: policy-template.json (snippet, 3KB)], [Attachment: latency-test-plan.md (7KB)]

See you on 1/19.
